2f41ac8.summary: Removes a CardEffect from the card's active effects and undoes what it changed (stats, traits, active ability, enchantment record). Then refreshes the health/attack/cost/trait UI and runs a death check for units. The decompiler merged in the tails of CheckIfDead, ToggleTraitIcons and CleanStatusAnims.
comments: Closure object captures removedEffect for the list predicates used below
Seems to bail out early when the effect has a flag set at offset 0x74 (nothing is undone)
Drop the effect from the card's active effect list
Branch on the effect's type id; each type undoes a different kind of change
Effect type 0x2d: a drop pod stat buff; only that type is handled in this branch
Effect carried a health bonus: subtract it from the drop pod health
Effect carried an attack bonus: subtract it from the drop pod attack
Redraw the attack/health figures on the card
Effect types 0xc, 0xf, 0x10 (enchantment-linked) or 0x28 (active ability)
Enchantment-linked effect: find and remove the matching ActiveEnchantment record
Removed enchantment was a quest (ids 0x28/0x78) and not jammed: broadcast quest resolved, reset counter
Type 0x28: restore the card's default active ability flag and clear the active ability ref
Clear status animations on the card UI and rebuild its trait icons (inlined UpdateTraitIcons)
Effect types 1 and 2 (stat changes) and 3, 5, 10 handled below
Type 1: health buff removed, so clamp current health down to the new max health
If the effect granted armour, take that armour away again
Type 5: reset attack and max health to the card's printed values, then clamp current health
Effect type 0x5a: falls into the trait removal code below
Trait-granting effect removed (types 3, 0x5a): drop the trait if nothing else still provides it
Trait is not a printed default trait and no other active effect grants it: remove it
Trait 0xe6 (drop pod): if the card no longer has drop pod, remove the drop pod
Trait 0x262 (pack): if the card no longer has pack, forget the last pack troops
Refresh health, attack, cost and trait icons after any change
Only units need a death check; other cards return here
Start of an inlined CheckIfDead: builds a debug log string, then checks whether the unit should die
Cards with zero starting health are ignored by the death check
Drop pod card in play with drop pod health at or below zero: destroy the drop pod instead of the card
Health still above zero: nothing dies
Card is not in a play state: warn and skip
Survivor charges left: use one (sacrifice trigger first if it is our turn) instead of dying
Card should become a remnant: run backlash actions and queue the transform instead of dying
Otherwise mark the card as waitingToDie and hide its can-attack glow
Decompiler jump target; calls here are the end of the inlined CheckIfDead
Decompiler glue: from here the code is the tail of BattleCardUI.ToggleTraitIcons (show/hide every icon)
Decompiler glue: from here the code is BattleCardUI.CleanStatusAnims, which clears status effect objects
Destroy or stop each matching status animation in the first dictionary
Same cleanup for the second status animation dictionary
Destroy the codex object unless the card still has quests (or clearAll was requested), then stop showing codex

2f2d7d4.summary: Removes a trait from the card's current and showing trait lists without triggering any game effects. Cleans up the trait's frame effects on the card UI, plays its exit animation, and updates the flying display.
comments: Closure captures the trait to remove for the Find predicate
Look up the trait data; if the card does not have it, nothing to do
Remove it from the current traits, and from the displayed traits if present
Fetch the trait's config (visual effects) from the trait collection
Stop and remove the looping frame effect for this trait on the card UI
Same for the one-shot trigger frame effect
If the trait config exists, play its exit effects
Effect kind 1 seems to be an exit effect: start the trait animation as a coroutine on the card UI
After removal, keep the flying visual in sync: losing flying turns it off
Losing vanguard only matters if the card still has flying
Card still has flying so the flying visual is turned back on
Update the card UI's flying display

2f3b994.summary: Adds a trait to the card's current and showing trait lists without triggering effects, unless the card already has it. The trait is created with the given hidden flag and default value.
comments: Check whether the card already has this trait
Already present: do nothing
Create a fresh trait data object
Add it to CurrentTraits (inlined List.Add)
Also add it to CurrentShowingTraits (inlined List.Add with resize)
Decompiler null check on a list or array

2f3e86c.summary: Removes a trait from the card's trait lists, logs it, and refreshes the card UI. Warns and does nothing if the card has no such trait.
comments: Find the trait entry; a missing entry or id 0 means there is no logic for it
Trait not found: log a warning and stop
Log the removal
Remove from current traits and from the showing traits if present
Remove the trait's status animation from the card UI
Trait id 0x3cf: redraw the attack/health figures
Trait ids 0x1cc and 0x28: update summon sickness animation and can-act state
Rebuild trait icons
Decompiler null check jump target

2f2f764.summary: Removes every active effect that grants the given trait, then removes the trait itself from the card (an inlined RemoveTrait). Refreshes the card UI afterwards.
comments: Remove all active effects tied to this trait
Inlined RemoveTrait from here on
Find the trait entry; missing means nothing to remove
Trait not found: warn and stop
Log the removal
Remove from current traits and from showing traits if present
Remove the trait status animation from the card UI
Trait id 0x3cf: redraw the attack/health figures
Trait ids 0x1cc and 0x28: update summon sickness animation and can-act state
Rebuild trait icons

2f2f658.summary: Starts or stops the summon-sickness animation and recomputes canAct and canAttack for the card. Also updates the can-attack glow. Ferocity and oath cards may act even while summon sick.
comments: Show or hide the summon-sickness animation on the card UI
Is it this card owner's turn?
Cannot act if it is not the owner's turn, not in play, already attacked (unless bloodthirst allows a second), or stunned
Otherwise it can act only when it is not summon sick
Store the result as both canAct and canAttack
Ferocity or oath cards can use abilities while summon sick, so canAct is recomputed without the sickness check
Same turn, in play and attack count rules, and not stunned
Summon sick ferocity/oath card: switch its attack type to Active
Show the can-attack glow only if the card can attack now
Ability availability is also queried here; result seems unused

2f43e90.summary: Returns whether the card has an extrinsic (granted by another card) effect from the given enchanting card, optionally matching the buff type and base enchantment card.
comments: No enchanting card given: nothing can match
Scan all active effects
Only extrinsic effects (those applied by another card) count
Effect's source card must be the given enchanting card
If a buff type was requested it must match
Base enchantment card must also match; then we have found one
No match, try the next effect

2f45718.summary: Returns whether the card already has an active effect equal to the given effect (same source). Used to avoid applying the same effect twice.
comments: Effects without an enchanting source card never count as duplicates
Compare against each active effect
IsSameEffect decides equality; heroCheck changes how heroes are compared

2f45814.summary: Returns whether the card has any of a fixed list of protective traits (ids 0xf0, 0x50, 0x136, 0xe6, 0x1ae), via the trait criteria filter. Builds the list on every call.
comments: Build the list of protective trait ids (each Add is inlined with resize handling)
Trait ids added: 0xf0, 0x50, 0x136, 0xe6 (drop pod), 0x1ae
Loop over the traits; once one matches, the flag stays true and later checks are skipped
Check whether this card meets the trait criteria for the current trait
Decompiler null check target

2f45a9c.summary: Returns true if the card died on the current turn, comparing its turnDied value with the battle manager's turn counter.
comments: Needs a battle manager to read the turn counter
Turn counter is an anti-cheat ObscuredInt copied out; compare with the card's turnDied

2f45b3c.summary: Returns true if the card died on the current turn or on the turn just before it.
comments: Died this turn
Otherwise re-read the turn counter and check whether it died exactly one turn ago

2f44078.summary: Returns the extrinsic effect on the card that came from the given enchanting card, or null if there is none.
comments: Scan active effects; returns null when the end is reached
Only extrinsic effects (applied by other cards) count
Effect needs a source card, and it must be the given enchanting card
Match: return this effect from the list (inlined List indexer)
Decompiler glued unrelated code after this point (List set_Item and a type-check helper); ignore it
No match, try the next effect

2f3c058.summary: Refreshes the trait icons on the card's board UI: hides all icons, then shows one per trait in the in-play ability list with its counter value. This is an inlined copy of BattleCardUI.UpdateTraitIcons; only units are updated.
comments: Clear existing status animations on the card UI first
Only units show trait icons on the board
Hide every trait icon slot first
Ambush on the opponent's card is hidden from us: stop here without showing icons
Get the list of traits to show while in play and store it on the UI
Loop over each trait in that list, assigning icon slots in order
Find the card's current trait data matching this list entry
If found, get its value with modifiers and turn on the counter on that icon
Initialize the icon with the trait sprite, value, and whether the trait is active
Decompiler glue: index out of range target; the code after is the tail of ToggleTraitIcons
Show or hide every icon according to a flag
Decompiler glue: from here the code is BattleCardUI.CleanStatusAnims
Destroy or stop each matching status animation in the first dictionary
Same cleanup for the second status animation dictionary
Destroy the codex object unless the card still has quests (or clearAll was requested), then stop showing codex
